title: ZTF 2018-2025 timing matches GR decay within 2.5 sigma in 7 of 8 measured ultracompact binaries, rejects a fast decay for ZTF J0538+1953, and shows a 26 times faster drift in ZTF J2055+4651
abstract: We measured the orbital decay rate (Pdot) of 14 known ultracompact white-dwarf and hot-subdwarf binaries (periods 6.9-56 min) with public ZTF DR24 photometry from 2018 to 2025. We used season-by-season template timing with bootstrap errors and compared the results with GR predictions from the published masses and with published ephemerides. ZTF alone detects decay at more than 3 sigma in 8 systems. Six of them agree with GR within 1.6 sigma of the combined timing and mass uncertainty. These include ZTF J1539+5027 (1.084 +- 0.007 times GR, consistent with its published Pdot) and ZTF J2243+5242 (0.99 +- 0.02, seven times more precise than the discovery value). ZTF J2130+4420 is 2.5 sigma above GR with ZTF alone and 2.1 sigma above GR when joined with published high-speed timings. For ZTF J0538+1953, ZTF gives Pdot = -(8.4 +- 0.6)e-12, and ZTF plus all published minima give -(8.48 +- 0.15)e-12 (1.16 times GR). This rejects the reported -(1.16 +- 0.22)e-11 (p = 1e-5 on ZTF alone). The published 2024-2025 minima also give -8.3e-12 when they are anchored to the 2019 ephemeris. ZTF J2055+4651, a mass-transferring sdOB + WD binary, drifts by about 300 s in 7 years. A quadratic gives Pdot = -(3.43 +- 0.25)e-11, 26 times GR. The drift is the same in g and r, with other templates, and in the ellipsoidal harmonic alone. Conservative mass transfer has the wrong sign. A light-travel-time orbit from a third body of at least 0.03 Msun fits equally well. Limitations: GR tests are limited by published masses (5-30%); six faint or low-amplitude systems give no constraint; the J2055 cause is not identified.

display.caption: ZTF-only orbital decay rate divided by the GR prediction from published masses for 14 ultracompact binaries (blue: ZTF, with 1-sigma timing error; orange band: 1-sigma GR range from mass uncertainties). ZTF J2055+4651 is off scale at 26.3 +- 1.9.

ZTF J0538+1953 eclipse O-C relative to the Burdge et al. 2020 linear ephemeris: ZTF epochs (this work, offset-matched), the eight CMO minima of Antipin et al. 2025 and the 2019 Burdge T0. The GR curve from published masses fits all data; the reported Pdot = -1.16e-11 does not fit the 2018-2019 ZTF epochs.

ZTF J2055+4651 O-C from the full template (blue) and from the template-free ellipsoidal harmonic (violet). Both show a 300 s drift that accelerates (quadratic Pdot = -3.4e-11, 26 times GR); the orange line shows the GR curvature.
